server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

layers.name: server
layers.note: The database outcome is pg_xact_status() and marker visibility on a second connection.

layers.name: protocol
layers.note: This run does not capture packets. A command tag inferred from node-postgres is that driver parsing CommandComplete.

layers.name: driver
layers.note: Driver observations are fields on the pg query result, or Client.getTransactionStatus().

layers.name: pool
layers.note: A pool is in the process. This scenario does not record a reset statement. The command tag is read from the client result inside the transaction call, before the connection is released.

layers.name: transaction_manager
layers.note: PostgresQueryRunner.commitTransaction is TypeORM's transaction operation. It stays in the framework layer so the record does not invent a second boundary inside one library.

layers.name: framework
layers.note: The application-facing call is the framework transaction API.

layers.name: application
layers.note: The application is the subject code in this experiment.

framework_observation.basis: DataSource.transaction threw: current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block. Driver statements: START TRANSACTION [resolved START]; SAVEPOINT typeorm_1 [resolved SAVEPOINT]; ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT ppcs_no_such_savepoint [rejected]; RELEASE SAVEPOINT typeorm_1 [rejected]; ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT typeorm_1 [resolved ROLLBACK].

application_observation.basis: DataSource.transaction threw: current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block. Driver statements: START TRANSACTION [resolved START]; SAVEPOINT typeorm_1 [resolved SAVEPOINT]; ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT ppcs_no_such_savepoint [rejected]; RELEASE SAVEPOINT typeorm_1 [rejected]; ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT typeorm_1 [resolved ROLLBACK].

interpretation.note: The wrapper rewrote TypeORM's ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT to a missing name before PostgreSQL saw it. That injection is client-side. The question is what TypeORM does with PostgreSQL's error and with the later COMMIT tag.

boundary_basis: The independent check could not establish the outcome. A definite application report is not assigned to a layer from this input.

evidence.statement: pg_xact_status() in progress, marker visible false, session idle in transaction, xid 35451.

limits: Java and .NET are not installed in this environment, so pgjdbc and Npgsql were not executed.
The system Python has no psycopg module, so psycopg was not executed.
No packet capture. A server command tag is inferred only when a driver command tag was observed.
TX-02's missing savepoint name and TX-03's withheld ROLLBACK are client-side injections.
